q: The full form of 'COFMOW', an organisation under the Ministry of Railways, is:

options.A: Central Office for Freight and Wagon Movement
options.C: Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops
options.D: Central Organisation for Maintenance of Wagons

e: COFMOW is the Central Organisation for Modernisation of Workshops, a unit of the Ministry of Railways that plans and executes modernisation of railway workshops and production units.

q: Most of the rails used by Indian Railways are rolled and supplied by the:
e: The Bhilai Steel Plant of SAIL in Chhattisgarh has a dedicated rail mill that rolls and supplies most of the rails used by Indian Railways.

q: The first full-fledged railway workshop in India, set up at Jamalpur, was established in the year:
e: The Jamalpur workshop in Bihar, set up by the East Indian Railway in 1862, is regarded as the first full-fledged railway workshop in India.

q: The WAP-7, the standard high-power passenger electric locomotive of Indian Railways, was developed by:
e: The WAP-7 three-phase passenger electric locomotive was developed by Chittaranjan Locomotive Works and is the standard high-power passenger locomotive of Indian Railways.

q: The full form of 'DMRC', which built and operates the metro network in the National Capital, is:
e: DMRC stands for Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, the joint venture of the Government of India and the Delhi Government that built and operates the Delhi Metro.

q: In Indian Railways, 'MEMU' trains, widely used for short-distance services, stand for:
e: MEMU stands for Mainline Electric Multiple Unit, self-propelled electric train sets used for short and medium distance mainline passenger services.

q: The full form of 'DEMU', the self-propelled train sets used on non-electrified routes, is:
e: DEMU stands for Diesel Electric Multiple Unit, self-propelled diesel-powered train sets used mainly on non-electrified routes.

q: In modern LHB coach rakes, the 'HOG' system for supplying power to the coaches stands for:
e: HOG stands for Head On Generation, in which power for coach lighting and air-conditioning is drawn from the locomotive itself instead of separate generator cars.

q: The 'CBC' couplers used for joining coaches and wagons in Indian Railways stand for:
e: CBC stands for Centre Buffer Coupler, the knuckle-type coupler fitted at the centre line of coaches and wagons for joining them together.

q: In railway track terminology, 'ballast' refers to:

options.A: The steel fastening used to fix rails to sleepers
options.B: The bed of crushed stone placed under and around the sleepers
options.C: The concrete bed of a platform
options.D: The top surface of the rail on which the wheels run

e: Ballast is the bed of crushed stone placed under and around the sleepers; it distributes the load, holds the track in position and provides drainage.

q: A 'fishplate' in railway track is used for:

options.A: Fixing the rail to the sleeper
options.C: Supporting the rail at a crossing
options.D: Joining the ends of two rails together

e: A fishplate is a steel plate bolted across the joint of two rail ends to join them together and maintain continuity of the track.

q: In railway signalling and train working, a 'block section' is:

options.A: The portion of a railway line between two consecutive block stations
options.B: A section of track inside a station yard only
options.C: The portion of track occupied by a stationary train
options.D: A reserved section of a passenger coach

e: A block section is the portion of a railway line between two consecutive block stations, which a train may enter only after obtaining proper authority.

q: In the older semaphore signalling system of the Railways, the indication to the driver is given by:

options.B: A whistle code sounded from the station
options.C: A movable arm whose position and colour convey the indication
options.D: A flag shown by the guard of the train

e: In semaphore signalling, the indication is given by a movable arm whose position by day, and colour of light by night, tells the driver whether to proceed.

q: The main purpose of a marshalling yard on Indian Railways is to:

options.A: Carry out heavy repairs of wagons
options.B: Receive, sort and re-form goods wagons into new trains according to destination
options.D: Sell unclaimed goods lying in the goods sheds

e: A marshalling yard receives incoming goods trains, sorts their wagons according to destination and re-forms them into new outward trains.

q: Passenger trains of Indian Railways have been standardised on which braking system, replacing the older vacuum brakes?
e: Passenger trains of Indian Railways are standardised on air brakes, which use compressed air and replaced the older, less effective vacuum brakes.

q: The Sanghamitra Express runs between SMVT Bengaluru and:
e: The Sanghamitra Express runs between SMVT Bengaluru and Danapur near Patna, linking Karnataka with Bihar.

q: The Tamil Nadu Express runs between New Delhi and:
e: The Tamil Nadu Express is the premier train linking New Delhi with Chennai Central.

q: The Karnataka Express connects New Delhi with:
e: The Karnataka Express connects New Delhi with KSR Bengaluru, the capital of Karnataka.

q: The Gitanjali Express runs between Howrah and:
e: The Gitanjali Express runs between Howrah and Mumbai CSMT, linking Kolkata with Mumbai.

q: The Pushpak Express runs between Mumbai CSMT and:
e: The Pushpak Express runs between Mumbai CSMT and Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh.

q: The historic Flying Ranee, among the oldest trains of the Western Railway, runs between Mumbai Central and:
e: The Flying Ranee, a historic Western Railway train running since 1906, operates between Mumbai Central and Surat.

q: The Poorva Express runs between Howrah and:
e: The Poorva Express runs between Howrah and New Delhi, one of the oldest trains on that route.

q: The Vaigai Express, a popular day train of Tamil Nadu, runs between Chennai Egmore and:
e: The Vaigai Express is a fast day train running between Chennai Egmore and Madurai in Tamil Nadu.

q: The Island Express runs between KSR Bengaluru and:
e: The Island Express runs between KSR Bengaluru and Kanyakumari, the southern tip of mainland India.

q: The Mangala Lakshadweep Express runs between Hazrat Nizamuddin (Delhi) and:
e: The Mangala Lakshadweep Express runs between Hazrat Nizamuddin in Delhi and Ernakulam in Kerala.

q: The Pune division of Indian Railways is a part of:
e: Pune division is a part of Central Railway, whose headquarters is at Mumbai CSMT.

q: The Vijayawada division belongs to which zonal railway?
e: Vijayawada division belongs to South Central Railway, headquartered at Secunderabad.

q: The Jhansi division is administered by:
e: The Jhansi division is administered by North Central Railway, headquartered at Prayagraj.

q: The Bikaner division is a part of:
e: The Bikaner division is a part of North Western Railway, headquartered at Jaipur.

q: The Lumding division belongs to:
e: The Lumding division in Assam belongs to Northeast Frontier Railway, headquartered at Maligaon, Guwahati.

q: The Thal Ghat, a steep gradient section climbed by trains with the help of banker locomotives, lies between:
e: The Thal Ghat lies between Kasara and Igatpuri on the Mumbai-Nashik route, where banker locomotives help trains climb the steep gradient.

q: Which of the following is the northernmost railway station of India?
e: Baramulla in the Kashmir Valley is the northernmost railway station of India.

q: The Saraighat Bridge at Guwahati is notable in railway history as:

options.A: The longest bridge of Indian Railways
options.B: The first bridge built across the Ganga
options.C: The first rail-cum-road bridge across the Brahmaputra
options.D: The highest bridge of Indian Railways

e: The Saraighat Bridge at Guwahati, opened in 1963, was the first bridge across the Brahmaputra and carries both rail and road traffic.

q: The all-India timetable published by Indian Railways for passenger information is titled:
e: Trains at a Glance is the all-India timetable booklet published by Indian Railways for passenger information.

q: The well-known tagline of Indian Railways is:
e: Lifeline to the Nation is the well-known tagline of Indian Railways, reflecting its role in carrying millions of passengers and freight daily.

q: Which country has the longest written Constitution in the world?
e: India has the longest written Constitution in the world, originally containing 395 Articles in 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.

q: The power of a High Court to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose is conferred by:
e: Article 226 empowers a High Court to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights as well as for any other purpose.

q: The provision for the establishment of an Inter-State Council to promote Centre-State cooperation is contained in:
e: Article 263 provides for the establishment of an Inter-State Council to promote cooperation and coordination between the Centre and the States.

q: The concept of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: The concept of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America.

q: The minimum age prescribed for a person to contest an election to a Panchayat is:
e: The minimum age to contest an election to a Panchayat is 21 years, as laid down in Article 243F of the Constitution.

q: The Governor of a State in India holds office:

options.A: During the pleasure of the President
options.B: For a fixed term of six years
options.D: During the pleasure of the Chief Minister

e: Under Article 156, the Governor of a State holds office during the pleasure of the President, though the normal term is five years.

q: The members of the Rajya Sabha from a State are elected by:

options.A: All the members of the State Legislative Assembly, including the nominated members
options.B: The members of the Lok Sabha elected from that State
options.C: The elected members of the State Legislative Assembly
options.D: The people of the State directly

e: Members of the Rajya Sabha from a State are elected by the elected members of that State's Legislative Assembly through proportional representation.

q: The Slave (Mamluk) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate was founded by:
e: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, a slave-general of Muhammad Ghori, founded the Slave or Mamluk dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in 1206.

q: The Mughal-era market control and price regulation system, under which prices of essential commodities were fixed by the State, was introduced by:
e: Alauddin Khalji introduced a market control system under which prices of essential commodities were fixed by the State and strictly enforced.

q: Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, is situated on the banks of the river:
e: Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, is situated on the banks of the Tungabhadra river in Karnataka.

q: The Harappan site which has yielded evidence of a ploughed field is:
e: Kalibangan in Rajasthan has yielded evidence of a ploughed field belonging to the early Harappan phase.

q: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal was introduced by:
e: The Permanent Settlement of land revenue in Bengal was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793, fixing the revenue demand with zamindars permanently.

q: The practice of Sati was abolished in 1829 during the Governor-Generalship of:
e: The practice of Sati was abolished in 1829 by a regulation of Lord William Bentinck, supported by reformers like Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

q: The Kheda Satyagraha of 1918, led by Mahatma Gandhi, was organised in support of:

options.A: Peasants demanding remission of land revenue after the failure of crops
options.C: Indigo planters resisting the tinkathia system
options.D: Workers protesting against low wages in tea gardens

e: The Kheda Satyagraha of 1918 supported peasants who demanded remission of land revenue because their crops had failed due to drought.

q: The first woman to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress was:
e: Annie Besant was the first woman to preside over a session of the Indian National Congress, at Calcutta in 1917.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All-India Muslim League.
2. Under this Pact, the Congress accepted the system of separate electorates for Muslims.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Lucknow Pact of 1916 united the Congress and the Muslim League, and the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims under it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wood's Despatch of 1854 is described as the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'.
2. It recommended the establishment of universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Wood's Despatch of 1854 is called the Magna Carta of English education in India and recommended universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.

q: Which State of India is popularly known as the 'Land of Five Rivers'?
e: Punjab means the land of five rivers, namely the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

q: Mount Everest, the highest mountain peak in the world, is known in Nepal by the name:
e: Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, is known as Sagarmatha in Nepal.

q: The Banihal Pass in the Pir Panjal range connects:
e: The Banihal Pass in the Pir Panjal range connects Jammu with the Kashmir Valley.

q: 'Project Tiger', the wildlife conservation programme for the protection of tigers in India, was launched in the year:
e: Project Tiger was launched in 1973 to protect the Bengal tiger and its habitat, initially covering nine tiger reserves.

q: The Pulicat Lake, a large salt-water lagoon on the Coromandel Coast, is situated on the border of:
e: Pulicat Lake, a large salt-water lagoon on the Coromandel Coast, lies on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

q: The highest mountain peak in South India, located in the Western Ghats, is:
e: Anaimudi, rising about 2,695 metres in the Western Ghats of Kerala, is the highest mountain peak in South India.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chitrakote Falls is popularly known as the 'Niagara of India'.
2. The Chitrakote Falls is formed by the river Indravati.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Chitrakote Falls in Chhattisgarh, formed by the Indravati river, is popularly called the Niagara of India for its wide horseshoe shape.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Tapi (Tapti) river rises from the Satpura range in Madhya Pradesh.
2. The Tapi flows eastwards and empties into the Bay of Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Only statement 1 is correct: the Tapi rises in the Satpura range in Madhya Pradesh, but it flows westwards and empties into the Arabian Sea, not the Bay of Bengal.

q: The Imperial Bank of India was renamed as the State Bank of India in the year:
e: The Imperial Bank of India was renamed the State Bank of India in 1955 under the State Bank of India Act.

q: The decimal system of coinage was introduced in India in the year:
e: The decimal system of coinage was introduced in India in 1957, when the rupee was divided into 100 naye paise.

q: Which of the following is generally regarded as the first bank established in India, in 1770?
e: The Bank of Hindustan, established in Calcutta in 1770, is generally regarded as the first bank set up in India.

q: The 'Yellow Revolution' in India is associated with a rapid increase in the production of:
e: The Yellow Revolution is associated with a rapid increase in the production of oilseeds such as mustard and groundnut.

q: The Minimum Support Prices (MSP) for agricultural crops in India are recommended by:

options.C: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices

e: Minimum Support Prices for agricultural crops are recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices, after which the Government takes the final decision.

q: The oldest stock exchange in Asia, established in 1875, is the:
e: The Bombay Stock Exchange, established in 1875, is the oldest stock exchange in Asia.

q: Which vitamin is essential for the clotting of blood in the human body?
e: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting because it is required for the synthesis of clotting factors such as prothrombin in the liver.

q: The disease goitre, marked by the enlargement of the thyroid gland, is caused by the deficiency of:
e: Goitre, the enlargement of the thyroid gland, is caused by deficiency of iodine, which is needed to produce thyroid hormones.

q: Baking soda, commonly used in cooking and as an antacid, is chemically:
e: Baking soda is chemically sodium bicarbonate, used in cooking as a raising agent and also as a mild antacid.

q: The metal used for making the filament of an incandescent electric bulb is:
e: Tungsten is used for bulb filaments because it has a very high melting point and offers high electrical resistance without melting.

q: Which planet is known as the 'twin sister' of the Earth because of its similarity in size and mass?
e: Venus is called the twin sister of the Earth because it is very similar to the Earth in size and mass.

q: The largest planet of the solar system is:
e: Jupiter is the largest planet of the solar system, bigger than all the other planets combined.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas.
2. The deficiency of insulin in the body causes the disease diabetes mellitus.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the pancreas, and its deficiency causes diabetes mellitus, marked by high blood sugar.

q: The green pigment present in the leaves of plants, which absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis, is:
e: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in the leaves of plants that absorbs sunlight and makes photosynthesis possible.

q: The famous Hindi poem 'Madhushala' was written by:
e: Madhushala, the famous Hindi poem built around the imagery of a tavern, was written by Harivansh Rai Bachchan.

q: The celebrated Bengali novel 'Devdas' was authored by:
e: Devdas, the celebrated Bengali novel about a tragic lover, was authored by Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay.

q: The first recipient of the Jnanpith Award, India's highest literary honour, was:
e: G. Sankara Kurup, the Malayalam poet, was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award in 1965.

q: Major Dhyan Chand, the legendary sportsperson of India, is popularly known as the 'Wizard of':
e: Major Dhyan Chand, who helped India win three Olympic gold medals, is popularly known as the Wizard of Hockey.

q: The Uber Cup is the world team championship for women in the game of:
e: The Uber Cup is the world team championship for women in badminton, held along with the Thomas Cup for men.

q: The National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas), marking the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is celebrated every year on:
e: National Unity Day, marking the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, is celebrated every year on 31 October.

q: The Waltair division, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Waltair division, headquartered at Visakhapatnam, is a part of East Coast Railway.

q: The Tiruchchirappalli division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Tiruchchirappalli division belongs to Southern Railway, headquartered at Chennai.

q: The Malda division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Malda division is administered by Eastern Railway, headquartered at Kolkata.

q: The Mysuru division is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Mysuru division is a part of South Western Railway, headquartered at Hubballi.

q: The Telangana Express runs between:
e: The Telangana Express runs between Secunderabad and New Delhi, linking Telangana with the national capital.

q: The Konark Express runs between:
e: The Konark Express runs between Bhubaneswar, the capital of Odisha, and Mumbai.

q: The Kamayani Express connects Varanasi with:
e: The Kamayani Express connects Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh with Mumbai.

q: The Paschim Express runs between Amritsar and:
e: The Paschim Express runs between Amritsar in Punjab and Mumbai.

q: The Gatimaan Express was originally introduced in 2016 between Hazrat Nizamuddin and:
e: The Gatimaan Express, India's first semi-high-speed train, was introduced in 2016 between Hazrat Nizamuddin and Agra Cantt.

q: The Himalayan Queen train runs between:
e: The Himalayan Queen runs between Kalka and Shimla on the narrow-gauge Kalka-Shimla railway, a UNESCO World Heritage line.

q: The Mahaparinirvan Express, a special tourist train of Indian Railways, is associated with:
e: The Mahaparinirvan Express is a special tourist train covering the Buddhist pilgrimage circuit, including Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar and Lumbini.

q: In Indian Railways, the computer application 'IPAS' stands for:
e: IPAS stands for Integrated Payroll and Accounting System, the computer application used by Indian Railways for payroll and accounts work.

q: The full form of IRSS, an organised Group 'A' service of Indian Railways, is:
e: IRSS stands for Indian Railway Stores Service, the organised Group A service responsible for materials management and stores in the Railways.

q: The full form of IRPS, an organised Group 'A' service of Indian Railways, is:
e: IRPS stands for Indian Railway Personnel Service, the organised Group A service dealing with personnel and human resource matters in the Railways.

q: 'Rail Bhavan' in New Delhi houses:

options.C: The headquarters of the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.D: The office of the Railway Board (Ministry of Railways)

e: Rail Bhavan in New Delhi houses the office of the Railway Board, that is, the Ministry of Railways.

q: Which city is the headquarters of three zonal railways — Eastern Railway, South Eastern Railway and Metro Railway?
e: Kolkata is the headquarters of three zonal railways, namely Eastern Railway, South Eastern Railway and Metro Railway.

q: The 'Pink Book' published annually by Indian Railways mainly contains:

options.A: The list of all railway stations
options.B: The details of the Works Programme, i.e., outlay on sanctioned works
options.D: The seniority lists of railway staff

e: The Pink Book published annually by Indian Railways mainly contains the Works Programme, giving details of outlay on sanctioned works.

q: In railway track, the sleepers laid below the rails primarily serve to:

options.A: Mark the boundaries of railway land
options.B: Support the rails, hold them to the correct gauge and distribute the load to the ballast
options.C: Conduct the return current in electrified sections

e: Sleepers support the rails, hold them to the correct gauge and distribute the load of passing trains evenly to the ballast below.

q: A 'loop line' at a railway station is mainly provided to:

options.A: Wash and clean the train rakes
options.C: Change the locomotive of a train
options.D: Receive a train so that another train can cross or overtake it

e: A loop line at a station is provided to receive a train so that another train can cross it or overtake it.

q: In railway working, a locomotive running by itself, without hauling any coach or wagon, is called a:
e: A locomotive running by itself, without hauling any coach or wagon, is called a light engine.
